feedback: If the child says the far lamp 'got smaller', clarify it is the same lamp — only the distance changed, just like the Sun and the stars.
Reinforce: the night stars are themselves huge suns; they only look like specks because of their vast distance.

If a child thinks all the stars are the same distance away or are stuck to the sky together, use the distance line to show they lie at wildly different, enormous distances — the Sun is simply the nearest.
activities.intendedInsight: Apparent size and brightness depend on distance; a bright object shrinks to a faint dot far off, which is exactly why real, enormous stars look like tiny specks at night, and the stars sit at wildly different huge distances rather than all the same distance.
learnerActions: Look at a bright torch or lamp held close up — note how big and dazzling it appears
Watch or walk it steadily farther away and describe how it shrinks to a faint point
Connect this to the night sky: discuss how distant stars look tiny only because they are so far away, not because they are small
Use a distance line showing the Sun as the nearest star and other stars placed vastly farther — at very different, huge distances
activities.title: A felt near-vs-far brightness comparison

feedback: If a child picks 'the Sun is the biggest/brightest star', explain the Sun only looks supreme because it is nearest — many night stars are actually far bigger and brighter (that ranking detail itself is for a later topic).

If a child sorts the Sun into a different category from the night stars, revisit that the Sun is a sky object and line it up alongside the stars as the same kind of thing, looking so different mainly because it is so much nearer.
If a child treats how big something looks as its real size, remind them the night stars are huge suns that only look like specks because of distance — apparent size is not real size.
activities.intendedInsight: A child who understands the concept says the Sun is an ordinary star seen up close and explains its appearance by DISTANCE, not by the Sun being the biggest star.
learnerActions: Answer: 'What is the Sun?' (a star / a planet / a moon)
Answer: 'Why does the Sun look bigger and brighter than other stars?' choosing 'it is the closest' over the distractor 'it is the biggest'
Describe or diagram the solar system as the Sun at the centre with all eight planets orbiting around it
Respond to the two-tier prompt: 'Is the Sun a star too, or a completely different kind of object? If it IS a star, why does it look so much bigger and brighter than all the others? Tell me WHY.'
activities.title: Explain WHY the Sun looks biggest
